label: second copy-phase step (input = first copied token, outputting orig[1]) in short sequences (L<=5)
explanation: Fires only at step t = L+1, right after <DEL>, when the input is the first fed-back output (orig[0]) and the model must output original token 1, and only for short sequences (L = 3..5). For those sequences it fires on essentially every one, with any token identity. Magnitude falls sharply with L: mean about 1.49 at L=3 (the top examples are all L=3), about 0.98 at L=4, about 0.43 at L=5, and a weak tail (about 0.07 of max) at L=6, which accounts for nearly all misses (0.1% of mass). It does not fire in the original phase, at the delimiter, at any other copy position, or for L>=7. Token identity has little effect; repeated tokens and digit count lower the rate slightly, only through their correlation with L.

issues: No real problems found. On the test split the predicate (recall_idx == 1) & (L <= 5) scores precision 1.0, recall 0.992, F1 0.996 and mass recall 0.999, with no false positives.

All 1272 missed steps on the test split are at step L+1 for L=6, with activations of about 0.06-0.09 of max. They hold 0.1% of the activation mass, which matches the 'weak L=6 tail' the explanation describes.
Widening the predicate to L<=6 drops precision to 0.675 and F1 to 0.806, so the cutoff at L<=5 is the right one.

The dev profile matches the claims. Activity is about one firing per sequence at recall_idx=1 for L=3,4,5. Inferred mean magnitudes are about 1.49 (L=3), 0.97 (L=4) and 0.43 (L=5), in line with the stated values. Firing is essentially zero for L>=7 (1 step at L=8), at the delimiter (0 steps) and in the original phase (2 steps). Activation-rate lift by in_tok sits at about 1.1x for every listed token, so token identity has little effect.
There is tiny scattered noise: 2 original-phase steps and 19 steps at recall_idx=2. This is not systematic.
